authMethods.label: Basic auth (Atlassian account email and API token)

usage.reason: The Confluence Cloud REST API has no per-user last-active or last-login field. The audit log (GET /wiki/rest/api/audit) only records administrative events such as space exports and group changes, and the analytics endpoints only give view counts per page, so neither shows who actually uses the product.

assumptions: Confluence has no admin 'list all users' endpoint in this source. I used the user search (GET /wiki/rest/api/search/user) with the query 'type = user'. The source does not confirm that this exact query returns every user, so it needs testing against a real site.
The source cuts off the search response, so I assumed each result has the person's details under a 'user' object (user.accountId, user.email and so on). I added the top-level fields as fallbacks.
The search may leave out deactivated users, and the source does not say how to include them. No status field is available, so status is not mapped.
Email and display name can be blank when the user's privacy settings hide them.

The source lists basic auth but does not describe it in detail. I assumed it means an Atlassian account email plus an API token. Basic auth is tied to a person, so it may stop working if that person leaves.
The listed OAuth 2 scopes are a minimal choice based on the endpoints used. Atlassian may also need an audience or offline_access setting, which the source does not describe.
The server is declared as your-domain.atlassian.net, so I used a subdomain connection field. Paths start with /wiki.
The search endpoint's maximum page size is not documented, so I picked 100.

There is no usable usage signal. The audit log is an event log, but it only covers admin actions, so I marked usage as unavailable instead of reporting misleading data. Reading it also needs the Confluence Administrator permission.
The rate limits are not stated in the source.

findings.message: Docs are on atlassian.com but the connector calls atlassian.net. Confirm this is the vendor's own domain, because credentials will be sent there.
